question.problem: Given that the random variable $X∼\text{Exp}(2),$ calculate $P(X<\frac{1}{6}).$ Round your final answer to four decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
An exponential random variable $X$ with rate $\lambda $ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\lambda {e}^{-\lambda x}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that

$$
X∼\text{Exp}(2).
$$

So, $X$ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}2{e}^{-2x}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate $P(X<\frac{1}{6})$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<\frac{1}{6}) & ={\int }_{0}^{1/6}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1/6}2{e}^{-2x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{e}^{-2x}{|}_{0}^{1/6} \\  & =-{e}^{-1/3}+{e}^{0} \\  & ≈0.2835\end{aligned}
$$
